why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but cracks are showing. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google is cutting 2027 shipments of a Broadcom-designed AI chip by about a fifth (neither company has commented), and Alphabet sold bonds at wider spreads than in May. After the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders.

Chip stocks fell for a second day on Wednesday: Nvidia closed about 3.9% lower at US$149.30 after dropping as much as 8% early, Micron fell about 7% intraday and Lam Research 6.5%, and the chip index was down more than 6% at one point before recovering much of it. The Nasdaq-100 briefly sat 20% below its record. Nvidia’s board investigation and a congressional probe continue, and Reuters has reported SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues (no finding of wrongdoing). On Wednesday S&P Global Ratings warned it could downgrade Nvidia’s credit rating over governance.

October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% a year (core 3.3%, above forecasts) and Q3 growth was revised up to 4.3%, so a 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is now about 98% priced, with another expected early in 2027 (25 Nov). The decision lands at 6am Thursday 10 Dec Melbourne time.

No dated default-swap figures since Friday 20 Nov, when Oracle’s protection was about 328 bp (above the 300 bp bursting threshold) and CoreWeave’s about 1,233 bp. A 25 Nov report cited new records of 356 bp for Oracle and 1,314 bp for CoreWeave, and SoftBank at 501 bp, but without dates for the readings. Oracle shares fell 4.8% on Wednesday.

Anthropic swung from as much as 13% below its US$83 IPO price early on Wednesday to close about 1.1% higher, still just below the IPO price. Analysts have cited its capital needs and lack of a credit rating so far. Nvidia’s US$118bn of customer guarantees, about US$105bn tied to one OpenAI campus, remains in focus. (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)

Closed about 4.81–4.85% on Wednesday, down roughly 6–9 bp, as investors bought bonds for safety during the tech rout even though inflation data were hot. Tech fell while yields dropped, a partial echo of the bursting pattern, but the broad market finished only slightly lower, so it is not the full signal.

US crude closed around US$84.1 on Wednesday (+2.5%) and rose about 1% more to around US$84.5 in thin Thanksgiving trade; Brent was about US$91.1. Oil remains well above pre-war levels, keeping inflation pressure on the Fed.

The high-yield spread widened to 372 bp on 24 Nov from 323 bp on 13 Nov, so the AI sell-off is starting to reach broad credit, though spreads are still far from crisis levels. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

Wednesday split the market again: the Nasdaq fell about 0.6% after a 4% early drop, while the Dow rose about 0.3% after erasing a 1,100-point fall, small caps rose about 0.7% and NYSE advancers beat decliners about 2 to 1. The S&P 500 slipped only about 0.25%. Money is rotating out of tech, not leaving the market.
